**Decision: CONTINUE.** Round 103 is planned: three small Lows in the export pipeline, and only the first changes behaviour. Nothing moved to მზადაა (ready) this round.

**What C proved in round 102**
- C passed round 102 in the browser with 0 bugs, and root published it as `b6c9716` on both remotes. `b6c9716` is the round 103 baseline.
- I closed five items in the backlog, based only on C's evidence:
  - **A-R88 #1:** the option card now clears the footer: 8 px above it, scroll 59.
  - **GATE101-S1, -S2:** the progress text is read once, for both WAV and MP3.
  - **GATE101-S4:** the doc 089 status line was fixed.
  - **INFO-B101:** C confirmed the garbled Georgian text was a Chrome DevTools display glitch.
- The root reviewer's new findings are filed as GATE102-S1 to S5:
  - S1 (other browsers and real screen readers) needs the Tech Lead, because only Chromium is installed here.
  - S2 is accepted as cosmetic.
  - S3 can't happen today.
  - S4 is a small type cleanup.
  - S5 (the doc 090 status line) is in round 103.
- The reviewer's architecture note is recorded as a signal only. I added it to the pending checkpoint request to root (addendum o); it doesn't block anything.

**Round 103 (decision record D-29z68)**
1. **GATE89-S3, WAV worker watchdog.** If the worker sends nothing for 30 s, the export stops once and shows a clear Georgian error. The timer restarts on every progress message, so a slow but healthy export doesn't time out; a fixed total limit would fail long projects on slow machines. When the worker reports its own error, that text is now added to the message.
2. **C-R90 gap, a missing cancel test (CU10).** The test is kept only if deleting the "cancelled?" check right before the downloads makes it fail 3 times out of 3. Otherwise no test is added, and I close the item by decision, because a user's click can't land in that gap.
3. **A-R87, test order.** The progress tests are split the same way the cancel tests already are, so a single test can run on its own without hanging.

A's files:
- `export-wav.client.ts`;
- additions only at the end of `export-wav.test.ts` and `export-cancel-ui.test.tsx`;
- lines 243–321 of `export-progress-ui.test.tsx`;
- doc 090 line 4, and a new doc 091.

The protected auth and purchase files are frozen and their hashes check out.

**What C checks**
- In real Chromium, C swaps in a fake worker that never answers or that reports an error. C then checks:
  - the error appears after 30 ± 2 s with the exact text;
  - the worker is stopped once;
  - nothing downloads.
- **Cancel:** the worker must be stopped exactly once in total, and no timeout error may appear later.
- **Slowed-down CPU (6×):** a normal export must still finish, and C reports the longest gap between worker messages.
- **Regression checks:**
  - real WAV and MP3 exports, and cancelling them;
  - no requests to the protected purchase or download endpoints;
  - anonymous `/studio-lab` opens and `/studio/*` still asks for sign-in.
- Single progress tests must pass when run alone. The full test suite is left to the root gate.

**Why this scope and not something bigger**
- **The regression round is due next.** It is 2 days since the last baseline (2026-10-21), and the rule needs 3. The next planning on or after 2026-10-24 will be the regression round, whatever round 103 leaves open.
- **No new features can be scheduled today.** FB-01 to FB-16 are all built and C has passed them in the browser. Everything that remains waits on something outside the loop:
  - the purchased-library mount needs the auth owner's release;
  - T12 and VISUAL-A start only after the original scope is confirmed done;
  - the Tech Lead manual checks are external.
- **Not COMPLETE:** Lows, the mount, the full regression, T12 and VISUAL-A are still open.
- **Not BLOCKED:** work that doesn't depend on anyone outside the loop remains.

The advisor was available and I used it twice. Its three fixes (test timing, the cancel pass condition, and the empty advisor section in `b-round-102.md`) are applied. I touched no app source; the store tree is still clean.
